arxiv-1810-00982.title: Primordial to Extremely Metal-Poor AGB and Super-AGB Stars: White Dwarf or Supernova progenitors? DOI: 10.1017/pas.2026
arxiv-1810-00982.creator: Pilar Gil-Pons 1,2, Carolyn L. Doherty 3,4, Jordi L. Gutiérrez 1,2, Lionel Siess 5, Simon W. Campbell 4, Herbert B. Lau, John C. Lattanzio 4
arxiv-1810-00982.description: Abstract Getting a better understanding of the evolution and nucleosynthetic yields of the most metal-poor stars ( Z ≲ 10 − 5 Z\lesssim 10^{-5} ) is critical because they are part of the big picture of the history of the primitive Universe.

arxiv-1811-09711.title: Parallel Adaptive Monte Carlo Integration with the Event Generator WHIZARD
arxiv-1811-09711.creator: Simon Brass, Wolfgang Kilian, Jürgen Reuter
arxiv-1811-09711.description: Abstract We describe a new parallel approach to the evaluation of phase space for Monte-Carlo event generation, implemented within the framework of the Whizard package. The program realizes a twofold self-adaptive multi-channel parameterization of phase space and makes use of the standard OpenMP and MPI protocols for parallelization.

arxiv-2102-03205.title: Swampland Geometry and the Gauge Couplings
arxiv-2102-03205.description: Abstract The purpose of this paper is two-fold. First we review in detail the geometric aspects of the swampland program for supersymmetric 4d effective theories using a new and unifying language we dub “domestic geometry”, the generalization of special Kähler geometry which does not require the underlying manifold to be Kähler or have a complex structure.

arxiv-2102-05597.title: Cutoff for non-negatively curved Markov chains
arxiv-2102-05597.creator: Justin Salez
arxiv-2102-05597.description: Abstract Discovered by Aldous, Diaconis and Shahshahani in the context of card shuffling, the cutoff phenomenon has since then been established for a variety of Markov chains. However, proving cutoff remains a delicate affair, which requires a very detailed knowledge of the chain.

arxiv-2209-03498.title: lim Ulrich sequences and Boij-Söderberg cones
arxiv-2209-03498.creator: Srikanth B. Iyengar, Linquan Ma, Mark E. Walker
arxiv-2209-03498.description: Abstract . This paper extends the results of Boij, Eisenbud, Erman, Schreyer, and Söderberg on the structure of Betti cones of finitely generated graded modules and finite free complexes over polynomial rings, to all finitely generated graded rings admitting linear Noether normalizations. The key new input is the existence of lim Ulrich sequences of graded modules over such rings.

arxiv-2307-05240.title: The filament determination depends on the tracer: comparing filaments based on dark matter particles and galaxies in the GAEA semi-analytic model 2023 The filament determination depends on the tracer: comparing filaments based on dark matter particles and galaxies in the GAEA semi-analytic model – 2
arxiv-2307-05240.creator: Daria Zakharova ID, Benedetta Vulcani ID, Gabriella De Lucia ID, Lizhi Xie ID, Michaela Hirschmann ID, Fabio Fontanot ID
arxiv-2307-05240.description: Abstract Filaments are elongated structures that connect groups and clusters of galaxies and are visually the striking feature in cosmological maps. In the literature, typically filaments are defined only using galaxies, assuming that these are good tracers of the dark matter distribution, despite the fact that galaxies are a biased indicator.

arxiv-2406-19346.title: Eliciting prior information from clinical trials via calibrated Bayes factor
arxiv-2406-19346.creator: Roberto Macrì Demartino, Leonardo Egidi, Nicola Torelli, Ioannis Ntzoufras
arxiv-2406-19346.description: Abstract In the Bayesian framework power prior distributions are increasingly adopted in clinical trials and similar studies to incorporate external and past information, typically to inform the parameter associated with a treatment effect. Their use is particularly effective in scenarios with small sample sizes and where robust prior information is actually available.

arxiv-2412-07931.title: On the Krull dimension of rings of integer-valued rational functions
arxiv-2412-07931.creator: M. M. Chems-Eddin, B. Feryouch, H. Mouanis, A. Tamoussit

arxiv-2502-06545.title: Universal Sequence Preconditioning
arxiv-2502-06545.creator: Annie Marsden, Elad Hazan
arxiv-2502-06545.description: Abstract We study the problem of preconditioning in sequential prediction. From the theoretical lens of linear dynamical systems, we show that convolving the target sequence corresponds to applying a polynomial to the hidden transition matrix. Building on this insight, we propose a universal preconditioning method that convolves the target with coefficients from orthogonal polynomials such as Chebyshev or Legendre.

arxiv-2506-07090.title: Open-Flavor Heavy Hadron Production in Heavy-Ion Collisions
arxiv-2506-07090.creator: C. E. Fontoura, G. Krein, A. Valcarce, J. Vijande
arxiv-2506-07090.description: Abstract We study the production of open-flavor heavy hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The hadronization in the quark-gluon plasma is described in the quark coalescence model. We evaluated yields and transverse momentum distributions. A simultaneous study of conventional and exotic hadrons is carried out. The Wigner functions are evaluated using hadron wave functions obtained from a single realistic quark model.

arxiv-2508-05119.title: The sixth order QED radiative corrections to lepton anomalies due to the fourth order vacuum polarization insertions within the Mellin-Barnes representation
arxiv-2508-05119.creator: L.P. Kaptari, V.I. Lashkevich, O.P. Solovtsova
arxiv-2508-05119.description: Abstract The explicit form of the sixth order radiative corrections to the lepton L \displaystyle L ( L = e , μ \displaystyle L=e,~\mu and τ \displaystyle\tau ) anomalous magnetic moment from QED Feynman diagrams with insertion of the fourth-order polarization operators consisting of either two closed lepton loops or one lepton loop crossed by a photon line is discussed

arxiv-2509-24393.title: Towards Safe Reasoning in Large Reasoning Models via Corrective Intervention
arxiv-2509-24393.creator: Yichi Zhang, Yue Ding, Jingwen Yang, Tianwei Luo, Dongbai Li, Ranjie Duan, Qiang Liu, Hang Su, Yinpeng Dong, Jun Zhu ♠ \spadesuit THU ♢ \diamondsuit RealAI ♣ \clubsuit CASIA
arxiv-2509-24393.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yichi Zhang, Yue Ding, Jingwen Yang, Tianwei Luo, Dongbai Li, Ranjie Duan, Qiang Liu, Hang Su, Yinpeng Dong, Jun Zhu ♠ \spadesuit THU ♢ \diamondsuit RealAI ♣ \clubsuit CASIA. Although Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have progressed in solving complex problems, their chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning often contains harmful content that can persist even when the final responses appear safe.

arxiv-2601-01597.title: The effects of star-gas interactions on binary evolution in open clusters PeTar ( 87 ) , McLuster ( 49 ) , numpy ( 26 ) , Matplotlib ( 31 ) .
arxiv-2601-01597.creator: Jixuan Yang(杨季轩), Lile Wang(王力乐), Xinyu Li(李昕宇), Meng Sun(孙萌), Long Wang(王龙), Rainer Spurzem
arxiv-2601-01597.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jixuan Yang(杨季轩), Lile Wang(王力乐), Xinyu Li(李昕宇), Meng Sun(孙萌), Long Wang(王龙), Rainer Spurzem. Star-gas interactions can provide gravitational feedback that influences the dynamical evolution of stellar clusters, through processes such as dynamical friction (DF) and its counterpart, negative dynamical friction (NDF). Using the PeTar code, we perform direct N N -body simulations of an open cluster initially containing 10 4 10^{4} stars, evolving within a gaseous medium spanning a range of ambient densities.

arxiv-2602-17180.title: A Fourier-Space Approach to Physics-Informed Magnetization Reconstruction from Nitrogen-Vacancy Measurements
arxiv-2602-17180.creator: Alexander Setescak, Florian Bruckner, Dieter Suess, Young-Gwan Choi, Hayden Binger, Lotte Boer, Claire Donnelly, Uri Vool, Claas Abert
arxiv-2602-17180.description: Abstract Reconstructing complex magnetization textures from nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetometry stray-field measurements presents a challenging inverse problem. In this work, we introduce a physics-informed method that addresses this by incorporating the full micromagnetic energy directly into the variational formulation. Built on a PyTorch backend, our forward model integrates an auto-differentiable finite-differences micromagnetic framework with FFT-based stray-field calculations and Fourier-space upward continuation.

pmc-11678108.title: Differential Transcriptional Landscape of Vero Cells During Dengue Virus 2 Infection in the Presence of Sinococuline
pmc-11678108.creator: Amit Garg, Rahul Shukla, Amit Kumar, Charu Aggarwal, Arnab Mukhopadhyay, Navin Khanna, Simone Peletto
pmc-11678108.description: Dengue virus (DENV) is transmitted by Aedes genus mosquitoes and is responsible for dengue fever (DF) and other severe diseases, posing a significant challenge to the global health system. Currently, anti-dengue pharmacological treatment options are not available. Earlier, we demonstrated that Sinococuline has potent anti-dengue activity and prevents virus infection.

pmc-12561852.title: Can We Successfully Discontinue Anti-Tumor Necrosis Factor-α Treatment in Children with Non-Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis? The Experience of a Tertiary Center
pmc-12561852.creator: Ekaterina I. Alexeeva, Irina T. Tsulukiya, Tatyana M. Dvoryakovskaya, Dmitry A. Kudlay, Ivan A. Kriulin, Maria S. Botova, Natalya M. Kondratyeva, Elizaveta A. Krekhova, Meiri Sh. Shingarova, Maria Y. Kokina, Anna N. Fetisova, Kseniya B. Isaeva, Aleksandra M. Chomakhidze, Christina V. Chibisova, Mikh
pmc-12561852.description: Background: Some patients with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) can successfully undergo withdrawal of treatment with anti-tumor necrosis factor alpha (anti-TNF-α) therapy, which may reduce economic and treatment-related burdens and the potential morbidity of treatment for at least 6 months. Currently, no guidelines exist on the appropriate withdrawal of anti-TNF-α therapy once clinically inactive disease (CID) has been achieved.

pmc-12700914.title: Synergistic antibiofilm activity of methylene blue and silver nanoparticle-mediated photothermal therapy against Enterococcus faecalis biofilm
pmc-12700914.creator: Eman M Fouad, Hossam Tawfiq, Soha Abdelrahman Elhady, Ali M Saafan
pmc-12700914.description: Biofilm formation by Enterococcus faecalis (E. faecalis) in root canals is a significant challenge in endodontic therapy, often leading to persistent infections and treatment failures. This research paper investigates the antibiofilm efficacy of methylene blue mediated photothermal treatment (MB-PTT), as compared to the sole effect of diode laser, PTT, and sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) on E. faecalis biofilms.

pmc-13030834.title: Structural Design of T-Cell Epitope-Based mRNA Vaccine Constructs Determines the Quality of T-Cell Immunity and Protective Efficacy Against SARS-CoV-2 in Mice
pmc-13030834.creator: Vladimir A. Gushchin, Andrei E. Siniavin, Andrei A. Pochtovyi, Alina S. Dzharullaeva, Dmitriy N. Shcherbinin, Anastasia S. Ungur, Amir I. Tukhvatulin, Inna V. Shuliakova, Denis A. Kleymenov, Elena P. Mazunina, Evgeniia N. Bykonia, Sofia R. Kozlova, Evgeny V. Usachev, Ilya D. Zorkov, Daria M. Grousov
pmc-13030834.description: Background/Objectives: Epitope-based mRNA vaccines represent a promising strategy for eliciting protective T-cell immunity against SARS-CoV-2 and as well as for non-infectious mRNA-based vaccines. However, how the structural architecture of vaccine constructs (including epitope arrangement, linker composition, signal peptide presence, and the combination of MHC class I and II epitopes) shapes the quality of T-cell responses remains poorly understood.

pmc-13162140.title: Genetic Testing by Age at Onset in Parkinson Disease
pmc-13162140.creator: Alexander Balck, Eva-Juliane Vollstedt, Ana Westenberger, Lara M. Lange, Joanne Trinh, Meike Kasten, Katja Lohmann, Norbert Brüggemann, Claudia Trenkwalder, Brit Mollenhauer, Roy Alcalay, Kamalini Ghosh Galvelis, James C. Beck, Peter Bauer, Christine Klein, Inke R. König, For the Global Parkinson’s
pmc-13162140.description: This cohort study evaluates the association between age at onset and family history of Parkinson disease in patients who carry pathogenic variants. Current recommendations for genetic testing in Parkinson disease (PD) prioritize patients with early age at onset (AAO; onset ≤50 years) and those with a positive family history (FH), despite limited data on the diagnostic accuracy of these criteria.

pmc-13469955.title: Mechanism of stress relief by deep-hole blasting in floor drainage roadways and its effectiveness evaluation
pmc-13469955.creator: Chen-long Yan, Lin-ming Dou, Zong-long Mu, Fang-zhou Lu, Lei-lei Jian
pmc-13469955.description: To address the Rockburst prevention challenges caused by the limitations of roof blasting in deep coal mines, the stress relief mechanism of floor strata was investigated through numerical simulations based on 195 field practices of cross-layer blasting in floor drainage roadways.

pmc-13639361.title: Global variability in colorectal cancer screening guidelines: panel composition and recommendations
pmc-13639361.creator: Koki Nakajima, Hiroaki Saito, Yoshitaka Nishikawa
pmc-13639361.description: ObjectiveColorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Although many countries have developed CRC screening guidelines, how CRC screening guidelines are developed across countries remains unclear. This study examined guideline-development funding, stakeholders, and their conflicts of interest (COI), and compared CRC screening recommendations across Group of Seven (G7) countries.

pmc-13643548.title: Shocked Beyond the Field
pmc-13643548.creator: Kyoung-Ryul Julian Chun, Melanie Gunawardene, Boris Schmidt
pmc-13643548.description: Corresponding Author The report by Saida et al1 in this issue of JACC: Case Reports further expands the evolving spectrum of coronary vasospasm associated with pulsed field ablation (PFA). Importantly, this case challenges the prevailing concept that PFA-related coronary spasm is primarily a proximity-dependent phenomenon caused by direct energy delivery adjacent to epicardial coronary arteries.

pmc-13680530.title: ASIC1a as an integrating node in ischemic neurotoxicity: crosstalk with NMDAR and TRPM signaling
pmc-13680530.creator: Ke Lai, Lu-Yang Wang
pmc-13680530.description: Ischemic stroke triggers acidosis, glutamate excitotoxicity and oxidative stress, which converge to disturb ionic homeostasis through several cation channels, including acid-sensing ion channel 1a (ASIC1a), N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) and transient receptor potential melastatin (TRPM) channels. Emerging evidence suggests that ASIC1a functions as a context-dependent integrating node: protons directly gate ASIC1a, glutamate and bilirubin-associated signaling can modulate ASIC1a-dependent injury pathways.
